Based on my analysis of the test image and available references:

**Test image features:**
- Stem node/junction covered in dark gray-to-black dusty/powdery fungal coating
- White fluffy mycelium patches visible in center
- Necrotic stem tissue underneath
- Powdery/dusty texture overall

**Reference comparisons:**
- Alternaria references were all microscopy slides or brown stem cankers (Bugwood_7) — poor visual match
- Gray_Mold Bugwood_27 showed brown leaf lesions; Bugwood_21 showed white fluffy mold on fruit (partial texture match)
- Sclerotinia Bugwood_14 showed mostly white mycelium with small black sclerotia — closer but dominant color is white, not dark gray
- Gray_Mold Bugwood_15 was microscopy

**Reasoning:** The dark gray, dusty/powdery sporulation coating on a stem node with visible white mycelium is most characteristic of Gray Mold (Botrytis cinerea), which typically infects at stem nodes and produces gray-dark conidia mass with white mycelium beneath. The powdery dusty texture and gray coloration match Botrytis sporulation better than the other candidates, despite the reference images being a partial match.
